title: DesignSpec
description: What Tinker (the AI designer) or the UI proposes. draft-service validates it, maps it onto a Draft template, runs the real Draft generator (MIT, Nguyen/Coelho/Kim 2026) with its feasibility gate, and returns a body contract (creature-body/1) with a spec sheet and trainability flags. Infeasible designs return HTTP 422 {error, gate, message, hints:[{field, direction, reason, value?}]}; apply the hints (value, when present, is a schema-valid fix) and resubmit. Owner: morphology agent (may tighten/extend bounds; keep this file the single source of truth, ai-service reads it at runtime to build prompts). Read x-designRules and x-actuatorFamilies before proposing a design. Only bodyPlan, basePreset and the quadruped/multileg block change the body; name, concept, skills and look never do.

name.description: Short creature name shown in the UI.

concept.description: One-sentence pitch in the user's words.

bodyPlan.description: quadruped = Draft's official four-legged template (3 joints per leg: hip roll, hip pitch, knee; legs fl, fr, rl, rr). multileg = radial or bilateral body with 3 to 8 identical three-joint legs (hip yaw, hip pitch, knee), generalised from the Flower crawler (robots/multileg).

basePreset.description: Optional: start from a preset's actuators and proportions, then apply the overrides below. cheetah/bear/giraffe are quadruped presets (Draft's experiment YAML), flower is the multileg preset. A design that gives ONLY basePreset (no overrides) is exactly that legacy preset at original size; cheetah and flower already have validated walking policies. Without basePreset a quadruped borrows its actuator family's archetype proportions (x-archetypes) and a multileg starts from a 6-leg radial crawler.

quadruped.description: Only for bodyPlan=quadruped. Metres. Omitted fields keep the preset/archetype value. Family-specific minimums for shoulderWidth and hipOffset are in x-actuatorFamilies.quadruped (bigger actuators need more room).

torsoLength.description: Trunk length (Draft torso_lx); the hips sit just beyond its ends. Trunk mass follows the measured quadruped trunk density, so big trunks are heavy.

torsoWidth.description: Trunk width (torso_ly); Draft widens the drawn trunk to cover the hip-roll actuators.

shoulderWidth.description: Lateral distance between the left and right hip-roll axes (shoulder_width). Must exceed the hip actuator diameter: micro >= 0.1, qdd >= 0.14, harmonic >= 0.13, geared >= 0.19.

hipOffset.description: Lateral hip link from the hip-pitch axis to the leg (Draft hip_roll_link_length); it must hold the hip-pitch and knee actuators apart: micro >= 0.065, qdd >= 0.08, geared >= 0.15, harmonic >= 0.19. Longer offsets widen the stance but add hip load.

lowerLeg.description: Shank length (lower_leg_link_length), ending in a sphere foot.

actuator.description: Actuator family, anchored on a catalogued part (x-actuatorFamilies.quadruped); Draft sizes mass, envelope and armature from its fitted trends and gates the result. qdd = quasi-direct-drive MIT U12 class, fast and springy (best for jumping, Cheetah-sized robots); geared = planetary RMD-X15 class, very strong and slower (Bear-sized); harmonic = strain-wave eRob110H class, very strong and very slow (Giraffe-sized, tall robots, no jumping); micro = CyberGear class for small robots (torso under ~0.4 m, legs under ~0.25 m each).

strength.description: Multiplier on the family's rated peak torque (speed and gear stay the part's). qdd must stay <= 1.35: the MIT U12 is already near the best catalogued QDD power density. Other families accept the full range. Stronger actuators are also physically larger.

multileg.description: Only for bodyPlan=multileg. Metres. Legs are named leg0..legN-1 counter-clockwise from the front (+X). Omitted fields keep the preset/template value (template: 6 radial legs, bodyRadius 0.15, coxa 0.09, upperLeg 0.18, lowerLeg 0.22, micro).

legCount.description: Number of identical legs. bilateral needs an even count. 6 legs give a tripod gait, 8 a ripple, 4 a trot, odd counts a wave.

arrangement.description: radial = legs evenly around a round hub (flower, starfish, octopus); bilateral = legs in left/right pairs along an elongated body, splayed from 45 deg (front) to 135 deg (rear) (insect, crab, millipede-ish). Needs an even legCount.

bodyRadius.description: Hub half-width. Hub mass grows with area; the hip-yaw actuators sit around its wall, so 7-8 legs need a bigger hub (see x-designRules).

bodyAspect.description: Length/width of the hub; >1 elongates the body forward. Good for bilateral bodies (1.4-1.9; 8 bilateral legs need >= 1.6); radial bodies with 7-8 legs should stay <= 1.2.

coxa.description: Hip-yaw to hip-pitch link; it must hold two actuators apart: micro >= 0.08, qdd >= 0.09 (>= 0.10 when strength > 1.2).

upperLeg.description: Thigh (hip pitch to knee). Long thighs raise the hip load: keep it at or below lowerLeg.

lowerLeg.description: Shank (knee to sphere foot); sets standing height.

actuator.description: micro = CyberGear class (12 Nm, light, default); qdd = MIT Mini Cheetah U8 class (17 Nm, faster, heavier). See x-actuatorFamilies.multileg.

strength.description: Multiplier on the family's rated peak torque; stronger actuators are larger (qdd above 1.2 needs coxa >= 0.10).

skills.description: Skills the user wants to train. walk is always first. jump needs a strong, light body: the body.json trainability.verdict.jump says whether the legs can push hard enough (qdd quadrupeds with a compact trunk are the best jumpers; harmonic bodies cannot jump).

look.description: Optional cosmetic look; never changes physics.

x-designRules: Give the block that matches bodyPlan (quadruped or multileg), never the other one.
basePreset must match bodyPlan: quadruped -> cheetah, bear or giraffe; multileg -> flower.
bilateral arrangements need an even legCount (4, 6 or 8).
Quadruped actuator families need room: shoulderWidth >= micro 0.10 / qdd 0.14 / harmonic 0.13 / geared 0.19 and hipOffset >= micro 0.065 / qdd 0.08 / geared 0.15 / harmonic 0.19.
Quadruped qdd strength <= 1.35 (power-density frontier of the best catalogued QDD).

The hip-yaw actuators sit around the hub wall and must not touch: 7-8 radial legs need bodyRadius >= 0.11 with bodyAspect <= 1.2 (radial legs bunch up at the ends of a long hub); 8 bilateral legs need bodyAspect >= 1.6 with bodyRadius >= 0.11 (or bodyRadius >= 0.17 on a round hub); 6 bilateral qdd legs on a round hub need bodyRadius >= 0.11. Other layouts work from bodyRadius 0.08.

Standing needs strong legs for the weight: micro quadrupeds should stay small (torso <= 0.4 x 0.25 x 0.15, legs <= 0.25 each); big hubs (bodyRadius > 0.2 or bodyAspect > 1.8) with long legs (upperLeg + lowerLeg > 0.5) are too heavy for multileg actuators. The body's trainability.flags say 'cannot-stand' (error) or 'may-struggle-to-stand' (warning) when this happens.
For jumping prefer a qdd quadruped with a compact trunk (torsoLength 0.3-0.45), legs 0.18-0.3 each and strength 1.1-1.35.
A design with only basePreset reproduces the legacy preset exactly; change any field to make a new body.

quadruped.qdd: cheetah preset proportions (torso 0.52 x 0.20 x 0.18, shoulder 0.16, hipOffset 0.10, legs 0.25/0.23)
quadruped.geared: bear preset proportions (torso 0.62 x 0.46 x 0.30, shoulder 0.38, hipOffset 0.18, legs 0.38/0.36)
quadruped.harmonic: giraffe preset proportions (torso 0.64 x 0.34 x 0.33, shoulder 0.24, hipOffset 0.18, legs 0.69/0.61)
quadruped.micro: pup proportions (torso 0.30 x 0.16 x 0.10, shoulder 0.10, hipOffset 0.06, legs 0.15/0.15)

x-archetypes.multileg: 6 radial legs, bodyRadius 0.15, bodyAspect 1.0, coxa 0.09, upperLeg 0.18, lowerLeg 0.22, micro; with basePreset flower: the Flower's bodyRadius 0.145 and its own 12 Nm / 20 rad/s / 12:1 actuator class

qdd.label: Quasi-direct drive (MIT U12 class, Cheetah preset)

harmonic.label: Harmonic strain-wave (ZeroErr eRob110H, Giraffe preset)
harmonic.useFor: tall, slow, very strong robots (no jumping)

qdd.label: Quasi-direct drive (MIT Mini Cheetah U8 class)
